stories.title: Pakistan Cricket Board Names Shaheens Squad for Asia Cup
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has revealed the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the upcoming 50-over edition of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. The tournament is scheduled to take place in Qatar from November 19 to 29. Defending champions Pakistan Shaheens are placed in Group B alongside India A, Nepal, and the United Arab Emirates. Abdul Samad has been appointed as the captain of the squad to lead the team through their campaign.

Opening their schedule, the Shaheens will play against the UAE on November 20 at the University of Doha Ground, which is the only day fixture for the team. Their remaining group matches are day-night encounters at the West End Park International Stadium, facing India A on November 22 and Nepal on November 24. The semi-finals are slated for November 26 and 27, with the championship final scheduled for Sunday, November 29. Group A consists of Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China, and Sri Lanka A.

The squad features a robust batting core alongside captain Abdul Samad, including Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf, and Shamyl Hussain, with Rohail Nazir designated as the wicket-keeper. Spin duties will be managed by Danish Aziz, Saad Masood, and Sufyan Moqim. The pace attack is headed by Mohammad Hasnain, supported by Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, and Muhammad Imran Randhawa.

Pakistan holds a strong history in the tournament, having won the last 50-over edition in 2023 in Sri Lanka by defeating India A by 128 runs. They also clinched the previous T20 edition title by edging Bangladesh A in a super-over thriller. Furthermore, Pakistan finished as runners-up in the opening two editions in 2013 and 2017, and secured victory in 2019.

stories.title: Argentine Ambassador Offers Agricultural Expertise to Pakistan
stories.summary:
The Ambassador of the Argentine Republic to Pakistan, Sebastián Sayús, visited the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry to propose Argentina's expertise in advanced agricultural machinery, grain-storage technologies, and post-harvest management. During his address, Ambassador Sayús pointed out that Pakistan suffers annual losses of 10 to 20 percent in grain production and 35 to 40 percent in horticultural produce due to inadequate storage and post-harvest handling. He suggested that modern Argentine storage solutions, such as silo bags and metallic silos, could significantly help Pakistan reduce food wastage and strengthen its agricultural supply chain.

The ambassador also identified promising areas for joint ventures and business-to-business partnerships across agriculture, dairy, and pharmaceuticals, highlighting Argentina's advanced capabilities in oncology product manufacturing. He stated that the Argentine Embassy is fully committed to facilitating commercial connections between companies of both nations to help identify reliable partners and foster mutually beneficial trade relations. Emphasizing the economic context, Sayús noted that Argentina's exports to Pakistan reached approximately US$247 million in 2025, while Pakistan's exports to Argentina stood around US$75 million. Agriculture contributes over 5 percent to Argentina's GDP and more than 23 percent to Pakistan's GDP, with Argentina positioned globally as the third-largest food exporter.

Responding to the proposal, KCCI President Talat Mahmood emphasized the necessity of strengthening bilateral economic relations through balanced trade and the diversification of exportable products. Mahmood stressed that Pakistan must actively explore avenues to expand its exports to Argentina and narrow the widening trade imbalance. Both sides underscored the importance of private-sector engagement and exploring new commercial opportunities to grant Pakistani exporters stronger access to the Argentine market.

stories.title: Democrats Win Key Senate Races in US Midterm Elections
stories.summary:
Media projections indicate that Democrats secured major Senate victories in North Carolina and Georgia during the US midterm elections, though control of the chamber remains undecided with millions of votes uncounted. Former governor Roy Cooper easily defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina to capture a Republican-held seat, marking one of the four net pickups Democrats need for a majority. In Georgia, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff defeated US Representative Mike Collins. Additionally, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia gubernatorial race against Republican Rick Jackson, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of the state.

The elections serve as a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term. Exit polls conducted by SSRS revealed that half of nationwide voters viewed the midterms as a chance to rebuke the president, three-quarters expressed anger or dissatisfaction with the country's direction, and 70 percent want Congress to establish more checks and balances. President Trump's approval ratings have hovered near career lows amid voter frustration over the war on Iran, higher fuel prices, and broader affordability concerns. Historically, the sitting president's party tends to lose ground in midterm elections.

To capture a Senate majority, Democrats face a narrow path requiring them to defend all existing seats while winning at least two traditionally Republican states. In the House of Representatives, where Democrats need a net gain of three seats to take control, roughly four dozen races had been called by Tuesday evening. Meanwhile, the US Justice Department deployed 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states, drawing criticism from Democrats who labeled the initiative potential voter intimidation. The Alaska Senate race also drew controversy following a New York Times report alleging that Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign helped recruit an independent candidate sharing the exact name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, prompting a Justice Department criminal probe.

stories.title: International Conference Explores Future Drivers of Asian Migration
stories.summary:
Scholars and policy specialists from Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, Nepal, the Philippines, and Sri Lanka gathered in Lahore for a two-day international conference titled 'Future Drivers of International Migration from Asia.' Organized by the Centre on International Migration, Remittances and Diaspora at the Lahore School of Economics, the event focused on ensuring that migration remains humane, orderly, and sustainable. Dr. Shahid Amjad Chaudhry opened the conference by urging Pakistan to diversify its economy, expand high-value services, and prioritize education, healthcare, and IT to generate domestic employment.

CIMRAD Coordinator Dr. Nasra M. Shah shared demographic figures indicating that 83 percent of the global population resides in their country of origin, 13 percent migrate internally, and only 3.7 percent cross international borders. Keynote speaker Dr. Anna Triandafyllidou described contemporary migration as a complex, non-linear phenomenon shaped by socioeconomic and technological transformations. Academic sessions explored various regional migration trends, including Nepal's reliance on labour migration—where remittances account for 33 percent of GDP—driven by unemployment, economic uncertainty, and climate disasters. Experts also discussed how limited domestic jobs and steady overseas demand sustain migration from the Philippines.

Regarding Pakistan, Dr. G.M. Arif noted that traditional migration to Gulf Cooperation Council countries persists alongside a rise in skilled migration to Western nations. He attributed these trends to economic instability, government policies promoting overseas employment, and persistent skills mismatches. Discussant Dr. Naved Hamid emphasized that demographic pressures and limited local opportunities mean migration pressure will likely remain high in countries like Pakistan and Nepal, underscoring the need for forward-looking policies and stronger international cooperation.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Lists Ningbo Green Light in Historic SPAC Deal
stories.summary:
Ningbo Green Light Energy Limited (NGLEL) has achieved a major milestone by becoming listed on the Main Board of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX). This marks the completion of Pakistan’s first-ever Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) transaction. The listing was officially celebrated with a Gong Ceremony at the exchange. The business combination was successfully executed through a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Lahore High Court on September 30, 2026, routing the target company LSE SPAC-I Limited into a merger with NGLEL with the structural assistance of LSE Capital.

NGLEL operates within the renewable energy sector, focusing on solar engineering, procurement, construction, system integration, and operation and maintenance services. PSX Director Ahmed Chinoy stated that the innovative transaction demonstrates alternative capital access for growth-oriented enterprises while establishing a precedent for future SPAC listings that support Pakistan's transition to renewable energy and economic ties with China. NGLEL Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Qasim emphasized that the platform enhances the company's ability to scale operations and build long-term value, supported by Director Technology Cheng Quan's vision of combining international technical expertise with local execution.

LSE Capital CEO Aftab Ahmad Chaudhry, who pioneered the SPAC framework in Pakistan, highlighted that the transaction validates the model as a credible and efficient public market entry pathway. He noted that navigating the regulatory landscape required substantial innovation and persistence.

The PSX noted that this initial SPAC listing broadens public investment opportunities and underlines the growing economic significance of the renewable energy sector in Pakistan.

stories.title: National Assembly Committee Slams Delay in Minimum Daily Wage for OPF Workers
stories.summary:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis has expressed strong dissatisfaction regarding the failure to enforce minimum daily wage rates for workers of the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation (OPF). Parliament approved these wage rates during the Federal Budget for 2026-27, yet four months later, the public-sector institution has still not applied them. Committee Chairman Syed Rafiullah criticized the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis for the delay, pointing out that private entities are required to comply immediately while public workers are forced to wait.

Federal Secretary for the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Nadeem Aslam Chaudhry explained that institutional procedure requires a meeting and formal approval from the Ministry’s Board. He assured the committee that a resolution would be passed in an upcoming meeting within days to finalize the rates permanently. The committee recommended that all subordinate boards establish automated mechanisms to implement federal wage increases immediately upon announcement, alongside demands for stronger financial protection, better salary packages, and improved workplace safety standards for mine workers and their families.

Addressing recent safety concerns, the committee reviewed a coal mine incident in Sorrange, Balochistan, noting that three provincial mines department inspectors and two labor department officials have been suspended. Authorities have lodged First Information Reports, issued show-cause notices to responsible companies, and distributed 34 compensation cheques to affected families, while the committee urged all provinces and Gilgit-Baltistan to increase financial grants for such incidents to Rs 3 million. Additionally, the panel requested detailed financial portfolios from departments under the ministry and deferred three legislative bills—the Employees’ Old-Age Benefits, Industrial Relations, and Emigration Amendment Bills of 2026.

stories.title: Sindh Energy and Climate Conference Demands Fair Benefits for Host Communities
stories.summary:
Experts, lawmakers, and community representatives at the Sindh Energy and Climate Conference (SECC26) have demanded significant reforms in the provincial energy sector. They stressed that the transition to renewable energy must safeguard local populations, guarantee electricity access, reinforce provincial autonomy, and ensure fair economic distribution. Opening-day discussions revealed a stark contrast between high energy production and poor public access, noting that residents living near major wind and power projects continue to face power shortages, environmental degradation, and scarce job opportunities.

Research presented by Uswa Ali Memon indicated that only 16 per cent of households residing near 36 independent power producers with 1,800 megawatts of capacity are connected to the national grid. Community members reported that corporate social responsibility initiatives remain weak and voluntary, while large-scale developments like the Thar coal projects have caused land damage from wastewater, coal dust, and noise pollution without delivering promised jobs or resettlement solutions. Speakers called for mandatory CSR funds, district monitoring committees, and mandatory free, prior, and informed consent for local populations.

Furthermore, participants advocated for decentralised energy governance under Article 157 of the Constitution to expand provincial authority via the Sindh Electric Power Regulatory Authority (SEPRA). Experts also promoted microgrids and minigrids to alleviate rural electricity shortages, while calling for international climate finance to be delivered through grants rather than loans to prevent worsening debt burdens.

stories.title: Jamaat-e-Islami Inaugurates Gulshan-e-Iqbal Projects and Criticizes City Mayor
stories.summary:
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) leaders inaugurated 25 newly constructed streets and a model neighborhood in Gulshan-e-Iqbal Town, while strongly criticizing the city mayor for urban mismanagement and incompetence. JI Karachi Chief Monem Zafar, District East chief Naeem Akhtar, and Town Chairman Dr Fawad Ahmed jointly opened the infrastructure projects, which included three primary roads inside the National Cement Society within Union Council-7.

During the ceremony, Monem Zafar claimed that while the broader city suffers from severe decay, the nine towns managed by JI function as successful development hubs. He highlighted that Gulshan Town is swiftly advancing on an ambitious initiative to build 1,005 roads and streets spanning 10 million square feet, alongside successfully restoring local parks and doubling school admissions. Zafar also criticized the ongoing University Road project under the BRT Red Line as a source of prolonged public distress due to delays.

Naeem Akhtar noted that the newly paved streets in the Cement Society are the first major infrastructure upgrades the area has received in 22 years. Dr Fawad Ahmed stated that the recently opened roads and smaller streets were completed in a rapid 11-day timeframe, urging local residents to help protect the new developments. The inauguration event drew a large gathering of local residents and municipal officials.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Grants Protective Bail to TikToker in Sialkot Stampede Case
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, also known as "Mr Patlu," in connection with a deadly stampede at his mehndi event in Sialkot. Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar issued the protective bail order, which lasts until November 10, enabling Jatt to avoid arrest and approach the appropriate court for legal remedy. Jatt arrived at the court in a wheelchair to surrender.

The incident took place on Friday night at the Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road, where hundreds of people had gathered for a mehndi and prize-distribution ceremony organized by Jatt. A stampede erupted when the stadium gates were opened, resulting in two deaths and 18 injuries. A first information report was subsequently registered on October 31 at the Motra Police Station against Jatt, his brother, the ground owner, six others, and between 40 and 45 unidentified security guards.

The case was registered under multiple sections of the Pakistan Penal Code, including provisions related to unintentional murder, mischief, rioting with deadly weapons, unlawful assembly, and disobedience to public servants, alongside the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. Advocates Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi and Barrister Raja Ali Abbas Jalap represented Jatt in filing the petition to prevent his arrest before reaching a competent court.

During the proceedings, defense counsel argued that while the FIR fell outside the Islamabad High Court's territorial jurisdiction, protective bail was necessary to ensure the suspect could travel safely to the court where the case was filed without being detained en route. The petition described the accusations as false and baseless, noting that Jatt had no prior criminal record. Justice Dogar acknowledged the temporary and limited nature of the protective relief, allowing the petitioner time to surrender before the proper forum.

stories.title: Government and Jamaat-e-Islami Discuss Measures to Ease Fuel Price Burdens
stories.summary:
The federal government and a delegation from Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan held discussions in Islamabad to explore ways of mitigating the impact of petroleum prices on the general public, particularly low-income families. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar led the government side in a meeting with the JI delegation, headed by Liaquat Baloch, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Several key government officials participated in the talks, including Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Inter-Provincial Coordination and Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah Khan, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the finance secretary, and the special secretary. The discussions focused on identifying practical options to extend financial relief to ordinary citizens facing mounting global economic pressures.

Both sides evaluated current energy pricing models and committed to sustaining consultations over the coming days to formulate a concrete course of action. Senator Dar emphasized the administration's dedication to safeguarding public welfare and resolving the financial hardships experienced by everyday citizens.

Additionally, the Deputy Prime Minister highlighted the necessity of cross-party political engagement and dialogue when addressing national economic obstacles. Official statements confirmed that the meeting involved candid exchanges on practical relief measures, specifically targeting vulnerable low-income households, with both parties agreeing to continue working toward a shared path forward regarding energy costs.

stories.title: Hyderabad Glass Bangles Industry Faces Severe Strain Amid Gas Shortages
stories.summary:
Representatives of the Hyderabad Glass Bangle Manufacturers Association met with officials from the Hyderabad Chamber of Small Traders & Small Industry to demand urgent action against ongoing gas load-shedding and low-pressure issues. Association President Haji Saleem Khan led the delegation to the Chamber secretariat, where he stressed that resolving these fuel shortages is vital for the survival of one of Hyderabad's key industrial sectors.

According to Khan, inadequate gas supplies continue to severely disrupt factory production schedules. He added that liquefied petroleum gas, which serves as an alternative fuel source, is virtually impossible to buy at the official rate of 294 rupees per kilogram, with market prices surging to approximately 560 rupees per kilogram. He urged the Chamber leadership to advocate strongly for the industry with relevant government departments.

Chamber President Nadeem Ahmed Siddiqui responded by criticizing authorities for consistently raising tax collection targets while failing to supply industries with necessary utilities. He pointed out that the livelihoods of over 200,000 people depend on the local glass bangles trade, warning that ignoring the sector's difficulties threatens the economic stability of numerous families.

Siddiqui reiterated that gas shortages, low pressure, and exorbitant alternative fuel expenses have placed immense pressure on manufacturers. He assured the Association that the Chamber will collaborate closely with them to lobby government forums and protect both the local industry and the workers reliant upon it.

stories.title: FPCCI and ASEAN Diplomats Host Roundtable to Boost Economic and Trade Ties
stories.summary:
The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry, alongside the Honorary Consulate General of the Philippines in Karachi, hosted the Pakistan-ASEAN Business Roundtable under the banner "Navigating Our Future Together." The gathering united ASEAN diplomats, government officials, and business leaders to foster deeper economic collaboration.

Key figures addressing the event included FPCCI Senior Vice President Saquib Fayyaz Magoon, FPCCI Committee on Diplomacy Chairman Hanif Gohar, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Director General Irfan Soomro as the chief guest. The diplomatic contingent was spearheaded by Philippine Ambassador and ASEAN Committee in Islamabad Chair Dr Emmanuel R Fernandez, alongside ambassadors and high commissioners from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Brunei Darussalam, with co-hosting support from Honorary Consul General Dr Imran Yousuf.

Magoon pointed out that while ASEAN represents roughly 680 million citizens and a combined gross domestic product exceeding four trillion dollars, bilateral trade with Pakistan sits between eleven and twelve billion dollars, with Pakistani exports remaining below 1.5 billion dollars. He proposed establishing a Pakistan-ASEAN Business Forum with an FPCCI secretariat, routine trade exhibitions, business-to-business exchanges, and closer cooperation in the halal economy, alongside reviews of existing trade agreements with Indonesia and Malaysia and new preferential trade pacts.

Gohar's keynote address introduced practical proposals for regional integration, including joint ventures in corporate farming, digital services, and transport logistics. His prominent suggestion was a one-year multiple-entry "ASEAN Business Visa Sticker" for qualifying FPCCI members, alongside restored direct airline routes connecting Karachi with Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, and Manila. Ambassador Fernandez welcomed the initiatives and promised to relay the proposals to ASEAN capitals, while other diplomats expressed enthusiasm for expanded business-to-business engagement.

Chief Guest Irfan Soomro reaffirmed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' backing for private-sector economic diplomacy regarding visas, connectivity, and trade pacts. The roundtable concluded with an agreement to draft a two-year Pakistan-ASEAN Business Cooperation Roadmap and establish quarterly meetings coordinated by the FPCCI Diplomacy Committee.

stories.title: Experts at SDPI conference highlight reforms for Pakistan's funding gap
stories.summary:
During the 29th Sustainable Development Conference organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute in Islamabad, experts emphasized that Pakistan requires fundamental structural reforms, mandatory corporate social responsibility legislation, and innovative financing to address its expanding social-sector funding gap. Adnan Pasha, an adviser to the finance minister, noted that international institutions like the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank expect tangible implementation rather than mere reform announcements.

Water experts at the event discussed the regional challenges of water security. Ambassador Shafqat Kakakhel, chairman of the SDPI board of governors, highlighted the Indus Waters Treaty as a crucial agreement that prevented major conflict. Meanwhile, former Federal Flood Commission chairman Ahmed Kamal pointed out that Pakistan must actively pursue its treaty rights as India advances various hydroelectric projects.

In another session, international partners praised Sindh’s post-2022 flood housing reconstruction program. SPHF Chief Executive Officer Khalid Mahmood Shaikh stated that construction has begun on roughly 1.6 million homes, with one million already completed. World Bank Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar and ADB Country Director Dr Emma Xiaoqin Fan commended the initiative for its beneficiary-led approach, which has also driven financial inclusion by opening about 1.7 million bank accounts.

Discussions also covered energy transition and labor rights. UNESCAP Director Mikiko Tanaka warned of hurdles regarding renewable energy integration due to seasonal variations and transmission constraints. Furthermore, Parliamentary Caucus Secretary Dr Syeda Shahida Rehmani stressed the importance of improving protections for informal workers, as climate change heavily impacts women and vulnerable groups.

stories.title: Iranian President Says Renewed Conflict Benefits No One Amid US Strikes
stories.summary:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated on Tuesday that a return to war would benefit no one, following reported United States strikes on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. The reported attacks occurred as American voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that could impact President Donald Trump's authority. Unnamed US officials described the operations as defensive, while Iranian state news reported five rapid explosions on the island. Meanwhile, US and Iranian officials continued indirect negotiations mediated by Qatar, with officials from both nations expressing hope for an interim agreement.

Chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that the Islamic republic was ready for battle with its finger on the trigger, asserting that Washington must prevent further escalation. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed that intensive indirect talks were underway, and US Vice President JD Vance noted that some progress had been achieved. A senior Iranian official mentioned that Tehran could reopen the vital Hormuz oil and gas transit route within two days if Washington fulfilled demands including ending the war, lifting oil sanctions, and unfreezing assets.

The broader Middle East conflict began in late February with major joint strikes by the US and Israel, but it has largely stalemated for months. Prior to the latest events, President Trump suggested a deal was possible and mentioned potential future targets in Iran, while maintaining threats of retaliation. In Tehran, authorities erected a prominent billboard featuring a photograph of the US president alongside a hostile message. Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi maintained that Tehran retains the right to legitimate self-defense following the recent strikes in the Hormuz waterway.

stories.title: President Trump Confirms US Carried Out Minor Attack on Iran
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump confirmed during a telephone interview on Tuesday that the US military had executed strikes against Iran. Speaking on the Fox News program "Fox & Friends," Trump stated that the action targeted a newly completed anti-aircraft facility. He characterized the military engagement as a minor attack that was carried out immediately after the installation was finished.

The confirmation from the American leader followed multiple media reports regarding a raid on Qeshm Island, situated within the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait serves as a crucial flashpoint in the ongoing Middle East conflict. The president's remarks on the Fox network provided direct acknowledgement of the operation from the administration following the initial reports from various news outlets.

stories.title: OGRA Announces Price Cuts for Petrol and High-Speed Diesel
stories.summary:
Consumers across Pakistan will experience relief at fuel pumps starting November 4, following an announcement by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority regarding reduced ex-depot prices for petrol and High-Speed Diesel. Under the updated rates, the price of petrol decreased by Rs5.45 per litre, establishing a new retail price of Rs369.06 per litre. Similarly, High-Speed Diesel saw a price drop of Rs3.68 per litre, bringing its new rate to Rs391.52 per litre compared to the previous Rs395.20.

The adjustment for petrol is tied to a new 30-day pricing mechanism where oil refineries contribute to the petroleum levy with a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, allowing for a substantial consumer-end reduction. For High-Speed Diesel, the price decrease is driven by international market trends, specifically a drop in the global HSD crack spread from USD 41.89 to USD 38.00 per barrel. International benchmark prices for petrol declined to USD 115.49 per barrel, while HSD benchmark prices fell to USD 112.20 per barrel. Ex-refinery prices and import costs adjusted accordingly in response to these global shifts and changes in Platts pricing.

Despite the retail price cuts, government levies and fixed profit margins for both fuels remain unchanged. Both petrol and High-Speed Diesel maintain a Petroleum Levy of Rs80 per litre, a Climate Support Levy of Rs5 per litre, dealer profit margins of Rs9.98 per litre, and oil marketing company margins of Rs7.87 per litre. The Inland Freight Equalisation Margin is sustained at Rs7.51 per litre for petrol and Rs5.08 per litre for High-Speed Diesel.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan to Close for Allama Iqbal Day
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan will remain closed on Monday, November 9, 2026. The closure is in observance of a public holiday declared by the Government of Pakistan. The holiday is held to mark the occasion of Allama Iqbal Day.

stories.title: Pakistani Government Adopts Dr Ishrat Hussain’s Institutional Reform Blueprint
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government has formally adopted former State Bank of Pakistan governor Dr Ishrat Hussain's institutional reform blueprint as the foundation for its national restructuring agenda. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb announced the policy shift during a Sustainable Development Policy Institute ceremony where Dr Ishrat received a Lifetime Achievement Award. Aurangzeb explained that the administration chose to build directly upon previous work rather than starting entirely from scratch, noting that he had personally requested the institutional reforms report to guide the program.

Although the strategy has been officially embraced, Aurangzeb cautioned that the execution across numerous federal ministries and attached departments will proceed in phases due to the vast scale of the proposed changes. He praised Dr Ishrat as a dedicated mentor whose integrity and public service have left a lasting mark on the country.

State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmad also lauded Dr Ishrat, crediting him with successfully transforming the central bank during his tenure that began in December 1999 amid severe economic sanctions, international isolation, and a balance-of-payments crisis. Ahmad highlighted how Dr Ishrat strengthened the central bank's autonomy, professional capacity, and technology infrastructure through the creation of a dedicated IT committee.

During his acceptance address, Dr Ishrat encouraged young Pakistanis to remain resilient and invest heavily in education despite prevailing economic uncertainties and challenges posed by intelligence technologies. He reflected on his extensive career, which included a twenty-year stint at the World Bank advising on international economic reforms, post-conflict assistance in Tajikistan, and establishing a sovereign wealth fund in Azerbaijan that grew to approximately USD 75 billion in assets.

stories.title: Bomb Threats Force European Flight Disruptions and Airport Searches
stories.summary:
Approximately ten European flights were subjected to bomb threats on Tuesday, resulting in the brief closure of a Warsaw airport and the scrambling of air force jets in Rome. Authorities confirmed that despite thorough ground searches following the safe landing of all affected aircraft at various European destinations within a span of several hours, no explosives were uncovered.

Irish budget carrier Ryanair bore the brunt of the disruptions, accounting for four of the targeted flights. Among the incidents, two separate bomb warnings were directed at flights heading to Warsaw, Poland. These included an SAS Scandinavian Airlines service originating from Copenhagen and a LOT Polish Airlines flight departing from Heathrow, according to official statements from Polish airport authorities.

Additional Ryanair services experiencing alerts included flights traveling from Lisbon to Rome, Dublin to Rome, and Dublin to Sofia, Bulgaria. The situation prompted the Italian air force to scramble fighter jets to escort Ryanair flight FR9611 from Dublin as it safely touched down at Rome-Fiumicino airport at 10:45 am local time.

In a related incident, a Wizz Air flight traveling from Bergamo, Italy, underwent detailed safety inspections after landing in Sofia at 0910 GMT following a separate security alert. A Bulgarian interior ministry spokesperson confirmed the inspection to AFP as security agencies across multiple jurisdictions responded to the coordinated wave of threats.

stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Dismissal of Ex-IB Employee Over Domestic Violence
stories.summary:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan has dismissed an appeal filed by Jawad Abbasi, a former Intelligence Bureau cook, upholding the Federal Service Tribunal's decision for his compulsory retirement. Abbasi had faced disciplinary action under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules of 2020 after being accused of setting his wife on fire, alongside allegations of being ill-mannered and short-tempered. Although acquitted in a related criminal case by a lower court, departmental proceedings established the charges against him.

A two-judge bench, headed by Justice Ayesha A. Malik and including Justice Shahid Waheed, who authored the judgment, emphasized that a woman's dignity is a fundamental constitutional value. The court stated that state employees have an obligation to respect this dignity, and a civil servant's private conduct is relevant when it impacts their suitability for public office and institutional discipline. The bench noted that domestic violence is not a private family affair behind closed doors, but rather a grave assault on life and human dignity.

The judgment highlighted that Pakistan's Constitution permits special protections for women under Article 25(3), supported by legislation such as the Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act of 2016 and the Domestic Violence Act of 2020. Furthermore, Pakistan is a party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women. The court underscored that burning women in their homes under the guise of kitchen accidents or suicide remains a serious and recurring social evil in the country.

The ruling matters because it reinforces the legal accountability of public servants for serious domestic violence outside the workplace, linking private conduct directly to professional integrity and state service standards.

stories.title: Parliamentary Panel Defers Electronic Transactions Bill Over Ongoing PPP Consultations
stories.summary:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication has deferred the Electronic Transactions Amendment Bill, 2026, once more. Chaired by Aminul Haq, the committee agreed to the delay after the Ministry of Law and Justice requested additional time to reach a consensus with the Pakistan Peoples Party regarding proposed legislative changes.

During the session, committee members voiced strong frustration regarding persistent poor internet connectivity across the country, highlighting that two years of parliamentary review have produced no meaningful improvements. Poor service and frequent signal drops were reported to affect major urban centers like Karachi and Islamabad, alongside smaller towns and remote districts. Pakistan Telecommunication Authority Chairman Major General Hafeezur Rehman stated that five show-cause notices were issued to telecom operators in the past three months, though penalty recoveries remain stalled due to court stay orders. He explained that prolonged power outages, lasting up to 16 hours daily in rural areas, heavily disrupt service quality.

Regarding next-generation technology, Rehman reported that approximately 70 percent of 5G services have been rolled out in Karachi, supported by around 2,300 upgraded telecom towers. Additionally, the Pakistan Digital Authority briefed the committee on the National Digital Master Plan, projecting that digital transformation could add between $60 billion and $80 billion to the gross domestic product over the next five years.

The decision to defer the bill is significant as it highlights ongoing legislative negotiations between coalition partners while citizens continue to face widespread digital and telecommunication infrastructure challenges.

stories.title: National Assembly Panel Defers WAPDA Security Force Bill Amid Alliance Differences
stories.summary:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Water Resources has once again delayed consideration of the WAPDA Security Force Bill, 2026, due to differences between the government and the Pakistan Peoples Party. Headed by Ahmad Ateeq Anwar, the committee also established a four-member subcommittee to investigate prolonged delays and heavy expenditures surrounding the long-pending K-IV water supply project for Karachi, while demanding a detailed report within one week regarding alleged water theft from the Kachhi Canal.

Deliberations revealed that the WAPDA Act of 1958 currently lacks statutory provisions for a security setup. Meanwhile, the K-IV water supply project has faced a delay of roughly two decades. WAPDA Chairman stated that the revised project cost is estimated at Rs171 billion, and while the first 64-kilometer phase is slated for completion this year, making it operational will require an additional 50 megawatts of electricity. Committee members questioned the continuous inability to finish the project despite substantial spending, prompting the formation of a subcommittee led by Muhammad Idrees.

The meeting also addressed water distribution issues in Balochistan and alleged unauthorized water withdrawals from the Kachhi Canal in parts of Punjab. Mian Khan Bugti argued that the canal represents Balochistan's legitimate right, while irrigation officials noted that individuals involved in illegal water withdrawals frequently utilize court stays to hinder enforcement. Furthermore, WAPDA's Chairman warned of declining national water-storage capacity, noting that storage has fallen from approximately 23 million to 13 million acre-feet over the past 52 years, contrary to World Bank recommendations.

This postponement underscores legislative gridlock and deep concerns over water infrastructure management, funding transparency, and inter-provincial distribution disputes in Pakistan.

stories.title: Senate Committee Requests Comprehensive Briefing on Prime Minister's UN Engagements
stories.summary:
The Senate Foreign Affairs Committee has requested a comprehensive briefing regarding Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's United Nations engagements, Islamabad's position on the Iran-US conflict, the Makkah Pact, and wider regional developments. Chaired by Senator Agha Shahzaib Durrani, the committee met in Islamabad to review regional relations, foreign office reforms, and Pakistan's priorities under its leadership roles in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the Economic Cooperation Organisation.

While members welcomed the newly appointed Foreign Secretary and praised his previous tenure as Permanent Representative to the UN, they expressed concern over the absence of the Foreign Minister from the proceedings. The committee reviewed the Prime Minister's recent UN visit, noting that the UN Secretary-General's recent visit to Pakistan reflected successful diplomatic outreach. The panel directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to provide detailed updates at the next meeting concerning regional security dynamics, including the Iran-US conflict and the Makkah Pact.

In addition to foreign policy matters, the committee examined administrative reforms within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding document attestation. Officials reported that general attestation, accounting for 65 percent of the workload, has been digitized via the Higher Education Commission database, while manual services remain available. Apostille attestation makes up the remaining 35 percent. To enhance efficiency, the chairman directed the HEC, NADRA, and the ministry to present an integrated e-attestation plan utilizing QR-code-based verification to reduce human interaction and delays.

The committee also received an in-camera briefing on current relations with Afghanistan and discussed leveraging Pakistan's leadership in the SCO and ECO to advance national economic interests, transit trade, and regional connectivity.

stories.title: National Defence University Delegation Visits Foreign Ministry in Islamabad
stories.summary:
A 126-member delegation representing the 28th National Security Workshop of the National Defence University in Islamabad visited the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday. The delegation was led by Major General Muhammad Raza Aizad during the official visit to the ministry.

Foreign Office spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan delivered a comprehensive briefing to the workshop participants. He outlined Pakistan's foreign policy priorities and key diplomatic achievements, focusing on the nation's dedication to building bilateral partnerships and advancing regional cooperation.

The briefing also highlighted efforts to promote multilateral engagement and contribute to international peace and stability. Additionally, the spokesperson discussed diplomatic initiatives aimed at advancing national interests and fostering dialogue on regional and international issues with friendly countries.

The presentation concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session. During this segment, the participants and officials engaged in detailed discussions concerning diplomatic outreach, foreign policy goals, and shifting regional and global developments.

stories.title: Six Family Members Shot Dead in Hangu Residence
stories.summary:
Six members of a single family, including two women and three young children, were shot and killed inside a residential property in Hangu district. The tragic shooting occurred on Tuesday in the Sarokhel area, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Doaba Police Station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

District Police Officer Salahuddin Kundi confirmed the identities of the victims at the scene, noting that the household head, Noor Rehman, was among those killed alongside the women and children. All six individuals died from their injuries at the location.

Preliminary police investigations suggest that the primary suspect is Noor Rehman’s nephew, who is reportedly a drug addict. According to the District Police Officer, disputes arose because the victim regularly prohibited his nephew from bringing friends involved in drug use into the house.

Law enforcement personnel secured the bodies and transported them to Doaba Hospital for necessary legal and medical processes. Authorities are currently examining all aspects of the case while conducting raids to locate and apprehend the suspect, who fled immediately after the incident.

stories.title: Coca-Cola Pakistan Wins Sustainability Award for Plastic Road Project
stories.summary:
Coca-Cola Pakistan received the prestigious Sustainability Award in the Sustainable Cities and Built Environment category during the 29th Sustainable Development Conference and 4th Sustainability Investment Expo. The Sustainable Development Institute organized the event in Islamabad.

Her Excellency Maja Derrous Mortensen, the Ambassador of Denmark to Pakistan, and Romina Khurshid Alam, the Coordinator to the Prime Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, jointly presented the honor. Dr. Faisal Hashmi, Senior Director of Public Affairs, Communications and Sustainability for the Coca-Cola Pakistan and Afghanistan Region, accepted the award on behalf of the organization.

The conference operated under the central theme of rethinking development in an era of disruption. The awards specifically acknowledge transformative projects that successfully implement scalable, eco-friendly, and climate-resilient solutions.

This recognition highlights a unique public-private partnership involving Coca-Cola Pakistan, the Capital Development Authority, and TeamUp or the National Incubation Center. Together, these entities collaborated to construct Pakistan's inaugural plastic road situated along Atatürk Avenue in Islamabad.

stories.title: Punjab Chief Minister Distributes Laptops and Scholarships in Attock
stories.summary:
Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif participated in a laptop and Honhar Scholarship distribution ceremony held at Comsats University in Attock on Tuesday. Students hailing from Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa also attended and benefited from the financial assistance.

The visiting students expressed gratitude to the Punjab government for expanding the scholarship initiative beyond provincial borders, noting that the aid helped them cover semester fees totaling nearly 200,000 rupees. During the event, the chief minister handed out laptops and scholarship checks while receiving portraits and sketches crafted by the attendees.

Across the Rawalidpi division, a total of 6,161 laptops were distributed. This allocation included 628 units for public university students, 257 for private universities, 461 for medical colleges, 375 for nursing colleges, 17 for special education institutions, and 423 for Higher Education Department colleges. Furthermore, the Honhar Scholarship Programme provided 2,590 scholarships valued at 196.97 million rupees within the division.

The broader scholarship initiative serves learners across public, private, and federally chartered universities, alongside special education centers and medical colleges. The chief minister has previously expanded the total laptop allocation from 40,000 to 112,000, with 48,292 units already delivered across Punjab districts. Additionally, the first three phases of the scholarship program have successfully aided 108,000 students.

stories.title: Minister Seeks Review of Wood Log Import Restrictions
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain has directed the Department of Plant Protection (DPP) to re-evaluate existing regulations regarding the importation of wood logs with bark. The initiative is intended to simplify operations for timber importers and align national practices with international phytosanitary standards. 

The review was requested by the All-Pakistan Timber Traders Association (APTTA) during a conference held after the inauguration of the Central Plant Quarantine Laboratory and the Federal Pesticides Testing and Reference Laboratory at the DPP. The meeting was facilitated by DPP Director General Yaseen Murtaza, with APTTA figures including former Chairman Sharjil Goplani, Moiz Kakkal, and Mushtaq Vali Mohammed in attendance. 

APTTA representatives argued that the Import Policy Order (IPO) 2022 and high Plant Protection Regulatory Order (PPRO) charges have created severe regulatory bottlenecks that threaten the domestic timber industry. They pointed to the International Standard for Phytosanitary Measures (ISPM 39), adopted under the International Plant Protection Convention, which encompasses round and sawn wood with or without bark and provides frameworks for risk management. 

The association proposed moving required treatments, such as fumigation and debarking, from pre-shipment to upon arrival in Pakistan under DPP and NAFSA supervision. They maintained that this change would eliminate excessive costs and logistical hurdles without compromising plant health safeguards, thereby facilitating legitimate trade.

The minister's directive responds directly to these industry concerns, aiming to ease timber processing operations while maintaining proper pest-risk management protocols under internationally recognized standards.

stories.title: Sindh Cabinet Lowers Wheat Release Price and Approves Investments
stories.summary:
The Sindh Cabinet has approved a Rs 500 reduction in the release price of wheat per 40kg, bringing the rate down from Rs 5,000 to Rs 4,500. Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon announced during a press conference that this change is anticipated to lower flour prices by Rs 17 per kilogram. 

During the meeting, the cabinet also greenlit a one billion dollar urban development investment program supported by the Asian Development Bank for five divisional headquarters, focusing on water supply, sanitation, drainage, and solid waste management. Additional financial approvals included Rs 502.409 million for Jamshoro district development schemes and Rs 2.993 billion to improve water supply and drainage in Nawabshah Town. 

Addressing infrastructure, Memon noted that construction on the Ghotki-Kandhkot Bridge over the Indus River has reached 75 percent completion via a public-private partnership model. The government also plans to introduce a Traffic Management Authority and a Smart Traffic Management System for Karachi, alongside strict enforcement against illegal number plates, underage driving, and unauthorized firearms.

On the political front, Memon stated that political gatherings require prior authorization and firmly ruled out any rallies on Shahrah-e-Faisal, specifically warning the Muttahida Qaumi Movement against attempting demonstrations there. He also discussed upcoming public transport additions, noting that more than 100 electric buses and double-decker buses are expected to arrive by the end of November.

stories.title: Saylani Trust Expresses Alarm Over Rising Malnutrition in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Maulana Muhammad Bashir Farooq Qadri, founder and chairman of Saylani Welfare International Trust, has voiced serious concern regarding the widespread prevalence of malnutrition and food insecurity across Pakistan. He described it as deeply troubling that millions of families struggle for basic nutrition despite the country's agricultural status. 

His remarks followed a report presented by the Ministry of National Health Services during a National Assembly Question Hour session. The findings indicated that hepatitis causes approximately 48,000 deaths annually, while over 50 percent of children and adolescent girls experience essential nutrient deficiencies. 

In response to these challenges, Maulana Bashir Farooq noted that Saylani provides hygienically prepared meals to about 200,000 people daily through its Dastarkhwan program. The organization also distributes over 152 metric tons of fresh meat monthly to more than 1.221 million beneficiaries and runs a school meal program for underprivileged children.

While acknowledging that these efforts address only a fraction of the national need, he emphasized the organization's moral and religious commitment to helping vulnerable populations. He concluded with an appeal to business leaders, industrialists, traders, and financially capable individuals to contribute toward providing nutritious food to deserving families.

stories.title: UBL Honored as Best Bank of the Year 2025 by CFA Society
stories.summary:
United Bank Limited (UBL) has been named Best Bank of the Year 2025 in the Large Banks Category by CFA Society Pakistan during its 23rd Annual Excellence Awards. The accolade recognizes the institution's sustained growth, overall financial strength, and continuous excellence within the banking sector. 

UBL maintains a significant financial footprint with a deposit base of Rs 6.5 trillion, a capital base of Rs 529 billion, a network exceeding 2,200 branches, and a workforce of over 35,000 employees. The bank emphasizes inclusive employment practices by maintaining a substantial female staff and creating professional avenues for young people in the country.

In addition to the top banking award, UBL earned recognition in three other categories at the ceremony. It won the Best ESG Reporting Award 2025, placed as runner-up for Corporate Finance House of the Year in Fixed Income for January 2025 to June 2026, and secured runner-up status for Best Digital Banking Services of the Year 2025 for commercial banks.

These multiple honors highlight UBL's comprehensive performance across corporate finance, digital transformation, environmental, social, and governance practices, and innovative financial service delivery to its customers.

stories.title: Novak Djokovic Overcomes Valentin Vacherot in Paris Masters Opener
stories.summary:
Novak Djokovic battled back from a set down to defeat Monaco's Valentin Vacherot 6-7(5/7), 7-5, 6-1 in the opening round of the Paris Masters on Tuesday. The victory marked a return to winning ways at ATP 1000-level tournaments for the 24-time Grand Slam champion for the first time since reaching the fourth round at Indian Wells in March. It also provided Djokovic with a measure of revenge against Vacherot, who had previously defeated the Serbian en route to claiming the Shanghai Masters title last season.

The hard-fought contest kept Djokovic's mathematical hopes alive for securing a spot in the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin later in November, where he currently sits 11th in the rankings. Following a tight opening set dominated by unforced errors and a tie-break won by Vacherot, Djokovic called for a medical timeout to receive treatment on his right shoulder. The brief pause disrupted Vacherot's rhythm, allowing Djokovic to seize control in the second set and comfortably dominate the decider to set up a second-round match against Rinky Hijikata.

In other tournament action, US Open finalist Ben Shelton delivered a commanding performance during the night session, defeating Britain's Cameron Norrie 6-3, 6-4 in just 71 minutes. Shelton's victory preceded a special ceremony honoring French player Gael Monfils, who retired last month at the age of 40. Meanwhile, 20-year-old Spanish rising star Rafael Jodar fell in straight sets to Casper Ruud, a result that officially secured Italy's Flavio Cobolli a qualification spot for Turin despite his withdrawal from the Paris event due to a leg injury.

Additional opening-round results saw Holger Rune exit the tournament following a 7-5, 6-4 defeat to Tommy Paul, while Matteo Berrettini edged 14th seed Brandon Nakashima in a tight three-set battle. Taylor Fritz advanced past Benjamin Bonzi, and 17-year-old French wildcard Moise Kouame was eliminated in straight sets by lucky loser Nuno Borges. Tournament play is scheduled to continue on Wednesday with top-seeded players Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz entering the competition at the round-of-32 stage.

stories.title: Bayern, PSG Win While Manchester United Pulls Off Dramatic Comeback
stories.summary:
European football heavyweights Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain secured victories on Tuesday in the UEFA Champions League first round. Bayern defeated Atletico Madrid in Madrid with second-half goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer. Meanwhile, PSG set a record by becoming the fastest team to score four goals in a Champions League match, cruising to a 6-0 victory against Villarreal at La Ceramica Stadium.

At Old Trafford, Manchester United engineered a stunning comeback against AS Roma. After falling behind early due to goals from Matias Soule and Donyell Malen, United responded when captain Bruno Fernandes scored a penalty in the 58th minute. Matheus Cunha then netted twice late in the match to seal a 3-2 victory for United, though his eventful night ended when he was sent off in stoppage time following an earlier yellow card for celebration.

Elsewhere, Barcelona earned a 3-0 home win over Aston Villa after Lamine Yamal opened the scoring early and Raphinha added a second-half double. Inter Milan matched that scoreline with a 3-0 victory against Feyenoord in Rotterdam, thanks to goals from Yann Bisseck, Pio Esposito, and Piotr Zielinski. Other matches saw Lask beat Slovan Bratislava 4-0, Bodo/Glimt draw 0-0 with Lille, Galatasaray defeat VfB Stuttgart 2-0 with two goals from Aleksey Batrakov, and Sporting Lisbon edge Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0.

Ahead of kickoff across Europe, stadiums observed moments of silence to honor Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, who passed away earlier on Tuesday. Following these matches, PSG leads the standings with 12 points, sitting ahead of a group of six teams on nine points that includes Barcelona and Aston Villa.

stories.title: Polls Begin Closing Across United States in High-Stakes Midterm Elections
stories.summary:
Voting centers started closing across the United States on Tuesday evening as millions cast ballots in midterm elections that could strip President Donald Trump’s Republican party of its control of Congress. Opinion polls showed Democrats favored to capture the House of Representatives, while a series of competitive statewide races will decide which party controls the Senate. The first polling stations closed in Indiana and Kentucky, with many other states following shortly after.

The election serves as a referendum on President Trump, whose approval ratings hover near career lows amid voter frustration over the war with Iran, higher fuel prices, and broader affordability issues. Trump urged supporters to treat him as if he were on the ballot, while Republicans targeted Democratic candidates, including Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Texas candidate James Talarico, over progressive policies and economic concerns. Meanwhile, prominent figures like Elon Musk heavily funded Republican efforts, including donations supporting Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Logistical issues surfaced in several locations, with machine malfunctions slowing down voting and ballot-counting in counties across Georgia, Iowa, Mississippi, and New York. To oversee the process, the US Justice Department deployed 1,000 election monitors and observers to all 50 states, though Democrats criticized the deployment as potential voter intimidation. Legal observers also warned that Trump might challenge unfavorable results.

The elections encompass all 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats. Democrats must flip at least three House seats and four Senate seats to secure majorities in both chambers. Notable contests include a turbulent race in Alaska involving candidate Mary Peltola and an independent opponent sharing the name of incumbent Dan Sullivan, alongside closely watched battles in traditional Republican strongholds.

stories.title: Pakistan Successfully Flight Tests First Locally Developed Air-to-Air Missile
stories.summary:
Pakistan has announced the successful flight test of its first domestically created air-to-air missile, named the Fa’az. According to a briefing from the military’s media wing, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), on Tuesday, this milestone signifies a notable progression in the nation's defense and aerospace technology.

The newly tested projectile incorporates an advanced terminal guidance system designed to engage enemy aerial threats at extended distances. Military officials noted that the integration of the Fa’az missile will boost the operational versatility of the Pakistan Air Force and reinforce the country's defense capabilities, reflecting the technical maturity and self-sufficiency of the domestic defense sector.

Top military officers, along with the engineers and scientists responsible for the weapon system's creation, observed the launch event. High-ranking government and military figures, including President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, extended their congratulations to the development teams.

This defense milestone closely follows another recent missile test by the Pakistan Army on October 13, 2026, which involved an extended-range variant of the Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic weapon system. Equipped with sophisticated avionics and navigation tools, the Fatah-2 Extended Range system utilizes unique maneuverability and trajectory characteristics to strike deep targets and pierce through hostile missile defense networks.

stories.title: پوپ لیو چہاردہم امریکی تاریخ میں ووٹ ڈالنے والے پہلے پوپ بن گئے
stories.summary:
کیتھولک مسیحیوں کے مذہبی پیشوا پوپ لیو چہاردہم نے امریکی شہری کی حیثیت سے وسط مدتی انتخابات میں ڈاک کے ذریعے ووٹ ڈال کر تاریخ رقم کر دی ہے۔ ویٹی کن نے جمعے کے روز تصدیق کی کہ شکاگو میں پیدا ہونے والے پوپ نے انتخابات سے قبل اپنا ووٹ کاسٹ کیا۔ پوپ کا اصل نام رابرٹ پریوسٹ ہے اور وہ شکاگو میں پیدا ہوئے تھے۔ ویٹی کن کے پریس آفس کے مطابق پوپ لیو نے امریکی شہری ہونے کی حیثیت سے اپنا حقِ رائے دہی استعمال کیا اور وہ اس سے قبل پیرو میں قیام کے دوران بھی ووٹ ڈالتے رہے ہیں۔

ویٹی کن کے جاری کردہ بیان میں کہا گیا ہے کہ پوپ لیو اس بات پر پختہ یقین رکھتے ہیں کہ جمہوری عمل میں حصہ لینا شہریوں کا حق ہونے کے ساتھ ساتھ ان کی اہم ذمہ داری بھی ہے۔ پوپ لیو کے پاس امریکہ اور پیرو دونوں ممالک کی شہریت موجود ہے جبکہ وہ ویٹی کن سٹی کے سربراہِ مملکت بھی ہیں۔

واضح رہے کہ ویٹی کن میں بادشاہت کا نظام نافذ ہے جہاں کوئی سیاسی انتخابات نہیں ہوتے۔ امریکی وفاقی قانون کے تحت بیرون ملک مقیم امریکی شہری ڈاک کے ذریعے انتخابی عمل میں حصہ لے سکتے ہیں۔ امریکی محکمہ خارجہ کے قوانین کے مطابق کسی غیر ملکی ریاست کے سربراہ کا عہدہ رکھنے والے امریکی شہری کی شہریت کا جائزہ لیا جا سکتا ہے لیکن اس بنیاد پر شہریت خودکار طور پر ختم نہیں ہوتی۔

یہ واقعہ اس لحاظ سے انتہائی اہمیت کا حامل ہے کہ پہلی بار ویٹی کن کے کسی سربراہ اور مسیحی مذہبی پیشوا نے امریکی انتخابی عمل میں براہِ راست حصہ لیا ہے۔ اس سے جمہوریت اور شہریوں کے حقوق کے حوالے سے ویٹی کن کے سربراہ کا نکتہ نظر بھی واضح ہوتا ہے۔

stories.title: UAE Enforces 15-Year Age Limit for E-Scooter Permits Starting 2027
stories.summary:
The United Arab Emirates has introduced new executive regulations that establish a minimum age limit of 15 years for individuals applying to ride electric scooters, e-bikes, and mopeds. Scheduled to come into force on January 1, 2027, the updated framework is designed to improve traffic safety, manage the rapid growth of micro-mobility, and ensure the protection of riders, pedestrians, and motorists alike.

Under the new rules, permits will remain valid for three years and can be renewed indefinitely. These credentials will cover multiple classes of personal transport. However, personal mobility devices are strictly prohibited on public roads meant for conventional motor vehicles and must only be operated on approved, designated routes. Additionally, all equipment must satisfy strict safety requirements, featuring forward-facing lights with high and low beams, rear red brake lights, braking capability on at least one wheel, and stable, safe tires.

The revised regulatory framework categorizes individual mobility devices into six distinct groups: traditional bicycles, electric bicycles, electric scooters, mini-motored bikes under 50cc engine capacity with maximum speeds of 45 km/h, skateboards, and mobility devices designated for the elderly and disabled. Commercial rental operators are also legally bound to meet these same stringent standards to maintain public safety.

Alongside vehicle regulations, authorities clarified pedestrian rules at intersections, stating that flashing green lights do not permit waiting riders or walkers to begin crossing, though those already in the middle may continue safely. This pioneering regulatory amendment underscores the UAE's ongoing efforts to cultivate safer and more structured urban spaces amid the expanding impact of micro-mobility on urban transportation.

stories.title: Ireland Expands Critical Skills List to Attract Global Talent
stories.summary:
Ireland’s Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment has updated its Critical Skills Occupation List by incorporating six additional professions. The policy change aims to draw high-quality international workers to bridge severe staffing gaps across crucial economic sectors, including agriculture, construction, healthcare, intellectual property, and the interactive gaming industry.

The expansion centers around the Critical Skills Employment Permit regime, which serves as a primary economic tool for securing global talent. The scheme allows highly skilled individuals to work in Ireland without undergoing a standard labor market test, while offering a streamlined pathway toward long-term residency, permanent settlement, and family reunification for successful applicants.

The six newly integrated occupations cover a diverse range of technical fields. They include agricultural science experts specializing in crop production research, project management and planning specialists for large-scale building initiatives, and regional public health optometry and vision care practitioners. Furthermore, the list now includes intellectual property professionals who manage and defend IP portfolios, geographic information system surveyors focusing on infrastructure and mapping, and advanced rigging specialists in the digital video games sector.

By continuously adapting its immigration policies to match real-time market demands, Ireland seeks to maintain economic competitiveness, support strategic infrastructure and technology sectors, and reinforce its standing as a premier destination for skilled emigrants globally.

stories.title: Pakistani Parliamentary Committee Reviews Export Scheme and Tajir Dost Program
stories.summary:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue convened on Tuesday to examine the performance of the Export Facilitation Scheme, the implementation progress of the Tajir Dost Scheme, and the broader economic consequences of border closures. The session addressed critical matters related to the nation's budgetary and economic policies.

During discussions regarding the Export Facilitation Scheme, committee members requested a comprehensive briefing detailing financial utilization, operational systems, eligibility requirements, and the program's actual contribution to boosting national exports. Lawmakers voiced concern over alleged misuse of the facility and questioned its efficacy given the lack of a corresponding rise in overall export figures, emphasizing that verifiable data must guide performance evaluations. Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani explained that the scheme lowers the cost of imported raw materials for export goods and promised a detailed follow-up report.

The committee also evaluated the Tajir Dost Scheme, expressing unease over lower-than-anticipated participation from retailers despite prior consultations with trade bodies. Kayani noted that the deadline for filing returns expired on October 31, paving the way for an enforcement phase involving penalties for non-compliant retailers. Consultations with the Federal Board of Revenue and the Attorney General for Pakistan have been conducted to ensure the legal soundness of these enforcement steps before they are submitted to the Prime Minister.

The meeting featured virtual participation from several members of the National Assembly alongside special invitees, including senior representatives from the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, and the Ministries of Finance, Law, and Justice.

stories.title: امریکہ کا فی الحال ایران پر فوجی حملے کا کوئی ارادہ نہیں، صدر ٹرمپ
stories.summary:
امریکہ کے صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے واضح کیا ہے کہ امریکہ کا فی الحال ایران پر حملے کا کوئی فوری منصوبہ زیر غور نہیں ہے۔ برطانوی جریدے کو دیئے گئے ایک انٹرویو میں انہوں نے کہا کہ ممکن ہے کہ حملے کی ضرورت ہی پیش نہ آئے، تاہم انہوں نے اس عزم کا اظہار کیا کہ اگر ضرورت پڑی تو امریکی فوج ہر قسم کی صورتحال سے نمٹنے کے لیے مکمل طور پر تیار ہے۔

صدر ٹرمپ نے دعویٰ کیا کہ ایران کے خلاف عائد کردہ امریکی بحری ناکہ بندی کی وجہ سے تہران کی معیشت کو شدید نقصان پہنچا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ جنگ سے پہلے کے مقابلے میں اب آبنائے ہرمز سے کہیں زیادہ تیل گزر رہا ہے اور واشنگٹن کو اس معاملے میں وہ سب کچھ مل رہا ہے جو وہ چاہتا ہے۔

امریکی صدر نے انکشاف کیا کہ ایران کے ساتھ اس وقت بالواسطہ مذاکرات کا سلسلہ جاری ہے جن میں افزودہ یورینیم کے ذخیرے کا معاملہ بھی زیرِ بحث ہے۔ انہوں نے مزید کہا کہ امریکہ تہران سے مسلسل بات چیت کر رہا ہے اور اب یہ دیکھنا ہے کہ آئندہ حالات کس سمت میں آگے بڑھتے ہیں۔

صدر ٹرمپ نے ایک بار پھر دہرایا کہ اگر حالات نے تقاضا کیا تو امریکہ فوجی کارروائی سے گریز نہیں کرے گا، لیکن فی الحال ترجیح سفارتی رابطوں کے ذریعے ہی تمام مطلوبہ نتائج حاصل کرنے کی ہے۔ اس بیان سے خطے میں جاری کشیدگی کے دوران امریکی لائحہ عمل کی عکاسی ہوتی ہے۔

stories.title: Seventeen Terrorists Killed and One Soldier Martyred in Balochistan Operations
stories.summary:
Security forces neutralized 17 suspected terrorists during two distinct intelligence-based operations in Balochistan on November 1, according to the military’s media wing. The actions took place in the Kachhi and Kharan districts following intelligence regarding the presence of individuals linked to groups designated as "Fitna Al Hindustan" and "Fitna Al Khawarij."

In Kachhi district's Sanni area, authorities prevented an attempted roadblock by initiating proactive measures, resulting in the deaths of ten militants and the seizure of various weapons and ammunition. A separate operation in Kharan targeted a militant hideout, triggering an intense firefight that left seven more insurgents dead alongside recovered weaponry.

During the exchange of fire in Kharan, 25-year-old Sepoy Hikmat Ullah, hailing from Karak district, lost his life. The Inter-Services Public Relations confirmed that clearance operations continue in the region to track down any remaining threats.

These security measures form part of the broader "Azm-e-Istehkam" campaign endorsed by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan. The initiative aims to systematically eradicate foreign-backed terrorism throughout the country through coordinated law enforcement efforts.

stories.title: Americans Cast Ballots in Midterm Elections Testing Donald Trump's Presidency
stories.summary:
Americans went to the polls on Tuesday to cast their ballots in a midterm election functioning as a nationwide referendum on US President Donald Trump. Analysts and polls predicted that Democrats would capture a majority in the House of Representatives and potentially take control of the Senate. These potential shifts could grant Democrats the authority to obstruct Trump's legislative agenda, halt judicial appointments, and initiate extensive investigations into his administration.

The elections involve all 435 seats in the House, 35 out of 100 Senate seats, and governorships across 36 states. Voter sentiment has been largely shaped by economic discontent, including soaring energy costs, inflation, and the ongoing conflict with Iran. Trump, whose approval ratings have hovered in the low 30s, defended his record on television by pointing to his tariff policies, immigration crackdown, and actions regarding Iran. Meanwhile, Republicans have characterized their opponents as radical socialists while promoting Trump's tax cuts and anti-migrant positions.

Campaign expenditures exceeded $11 billion in political advertising, bolstered by substantial financial backing from billionaire Elon Musk for Republican initiatives. More than 57 million citizens participated through early voting. Concerns grew regarding the potential non-acceptance of results by Republicans, given Trump's repeated, unsubstantiated allegations of widespread voter fraud. The Justice Department deployed approximately 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states for the first time in history, an effort that drew criticism from Democrats over potential voter intimidation.

Legal battles preceded Election Day, including a Justice Department lawsuit to block certification of the Alaska Senate race and an emergency bid rejected by the Supreme Court regarding California mail-in ballots. Trump indicated that if he loses congressional control, he would rely on his veto power, though he left open the possibility of future deals with Democrats.

stories.title: امریکی انتخابات کے ابتدائی نتائج میں ڈیموکریٹک پارٹی کے امیدواروں کی کامیابیاں
stories.summary:
امریکہ میں پولنگ کا وقت ختم ہونے کے بعد ووٹوں کی گنتی کا سلسلہ جاری ہے اور ابتدائی نتائج کے مطابق ڈیموکریٹک پارٹی کے امیدواروں نے اہم نشستیں حاصل کر لی ہیں۔ امریکی میڈیا کے مطابق ریاست ورجینیا سے ڈیموکریٹک سینیٹر مارک وارنر نے ریپبلکن حریف برٹ میزوساوا کو شکست دے کر ایوانِ بالا یعنی سینیٹ میں اپنی چوتھی مدت کامیابی کے ساتھ حاصل کر لی ہے۔

اس کے علاوہ فلوریڈا کے 20 ویں کانگریشنل ڈسٹرکٹ سے ڈیموکریٹک رہنما ڈیبی واسرمین شلٹز نے اپنے ریپبلکن حریف برینٹ اینڈرسن کو ہرا کر ایوانِ نمائندگان میں اپنی نشست برقرار رکھی۔ اسی طرح ریاست کینٹکی کے تیسرے کانگریشنل ڈسٹرکٹ سے تعلق رکھنے والے ڈیموکریٹک رہنما مورگن میک گاروی نے بھی امریکی ایوانِ نمائندگان کی نشست پر دوبارہ کامیابی اپنے نام کی۔

ریاست جارجیا کے 13 ویں کانگریشنل ڈسٹرکٹ سے ڈیموکریٹک امیدوار جیسمین کلارک نے بھی کامیابی حاصل کرتے ہوئے ایوانِ نمائندگان کی نشست پر قبضہ جما لیا۔ مختلف امریکی ریاستوں میں ووٹوں کی گنتی کا عمل تاحال جاری ہے اور جیسے جیسے نتائج سامنے آ رہے ہیں، کانگریس کے دونوں ایوانوں یعنی بالا اور زیریں میں تمام سیاسی جماعتوں کی پوزیشن مزید واضح ہوتی جا رہی ہے۔

ان ابتدائی نتائج سے امریکہ کی سیاسی صورتحال اور قانون ساز اداروں میں طاقت کا توازن تبدیل ہوتا دکھائی دے رہا ہے۔ انتخابی عمل مکمل ہونے کے بعد ہی یہ واضح ہو سکے گا کہ حتمی طور پر کون سی جماعت ایوانوں میں اکثریت حاصل کرنے میں کامیاب ہوتی ہے۔

stories.title: Security Forces Eliminate 17 Terrorists During Balochistan Intelligence-Based Operations
stories.summary:
Pakistani security forces neutralized 17 terrorists identified with groups labeled as Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij during two separate intelligence-based operations in the Kachhi and Kharan districts of Balochistan, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

The first operation took place in the Sani area of Kachhi district, where troops confronted terrorists attempting to obstruct a road with barriers. Security personnel killed 10 insurgents and seized various weapons and ammunition from them. A second operation in Kharan district involved the destruction of a militant hideout, resulting in the deaths of seven additional terrorists following an intense exchange of gunfire.

During the fierce firefight in Kharan, Sepoy Hikmatullah lost his life, making the ultimate sacrifice for the nation. Military authorities confirmed that search and clearance operations remained active in both regions to neutralize any lingering threats.

The armed forces continue their counterterrorism efforts under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, aiming to eradicate foreign-sponsored terrorism throughout the country.

stories.title: US Voters Head to Polls for Midterm Elections Amid Uncertain Senate Control
stories.summary:
Voters across the United States participated in Tuesday's midterm elections to decide the trajectory of President Donald Trump's second term. Surveys and nonpartisan analysts indicated that Democrats were favored to capture the House of Representatives, whereas control of the Senate remained closely contested across roughly ten competitive statewide races in traditional Republican strongholds.

The elections serve as a direct referendum on Trump, whose approval ratings languish near record lows due to voter backlash against the conflict with Iran and climbing fuel prices. Trump urged supporters to treat him as though he were on the ballot, while Democrats echoed that framing. Economic affordability dominated voter concerns, overshadowing Republican efforts to label Democratic candidates as radical or communist. In Michigan, progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed engaged in a high-profile Senate race against Republican Mike Rogers, while Alaska experienced turmoil regarding a third candidate sharing the name of Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Tensions surrounding election integrity prompted the Justice Department to deploy 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states, marking the largest monitoring effort in history. Democrats criticized the deployment as potential voter intimidation, noting that two-thirds of targeted jurisdictions supported Kamala Harris in 2024. The administration also pursued legal actions in Alaska and California regarding ballots, though courts blocked or rejected those specific efforts.

Altogether, all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are contested. Democrats need to flip at least three House seats and four Senate seats to secure majorities, requiring victories in multiple states that strongly favored Trump in the previous presidential election.

stories.title: Karachi Port Receives Second Wheat Shipment as Imports Exceed 110,000 Tonnes
stories.summary:
A second vessel carrying imported wheat arrived at Karachi Port, pushing Pakistan's total received wheat imports past 110,000 tonnes and offering potential relief from ongoing supply concerns. The ship, named MV Great Rainbow, docked at berths 16 and 17 with a cargo of 59,132 tonnes destined for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with unloading operations immediately underway.

This import effort is managed by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) through two separate vessels to satisfy national food requirements and stabilize supplies. The initial shipment carrying 51,000 tonnes designated for Punjab arrived at the same port on October 28. Authorities anticipate that these incoming shipments will improve overall availability and lead to a decrease in the market prices of wheat and flour nationwide.

In tandem with these imports, Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain chaired a high-level meeting with private seed companies and the National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority (NSDRA). He urged seed providers to lower prices to assist small farmers facing high costs for agricultural inputs like fertilizer and irrigation. Furthermore, Hussain instructed the NSDRA to guarantee the smooth inter-provincial transit of certified seeds to ensure timely sowing during the agricultural season.

stories.title: Australia Considers Stricter Financial Rules and Standards for Student Visas
stories.summary:
Australia is reviewing its international student visa program to implement stricter financial standards and thresholds aimed at managing immigration levels and addressing non-genuine applicants. Under the proposed changes, international applicants might face rigorous financial verification processes, requiring tangible proof through direct deposits or restricted fund transfers regardless of their study code's risk level. Additionally, authorities plan to conduct new genuine student evaluations to thoroughly examine course histories, career intentions, and motivations for selecting specific programs.

These discussion points form part of a broader package of sweeping Australian immigration reforms.
